title: Industry alignment briefs — core use cases & positioning
content:
Purpose:
Quick, playbook-style briefs to align messaging and early GTM experiments across five prioritized verticals. This is intentionally lightweight: callouts for product requirements, competitive threats, suggested hooks, and 8-week launch experiments.

Overview (one-sentence frame):
Customers in regulated and mission-critical verticals care more about predictable economics and operational guarantees than raw model novelty. Position Redwood as the inference runtime that shifts orgs from model maintenance to reliable, cost-predictable serving.

Format note: where possible we propose a simple 3-line customer narrative + 3 positioning pillars + top 3 competitor risks + quick experiment ideas and metrics.

1) Fintech (payments, lending, wealth)
- Core JTBD: reduce latency and cost for high-throughput customer-facing NLP (fraud scoring, KYC triage, conversational assistants) while keeping auditability and deterministic outputs for compliance.
- Customer archetype: Platform engineering or ML infra owners at scale-ups and banks; high throughput, predictable peaks (e.g., end of month), security-first.
- 3-line narrative: "Integrate LLM features into payment flows without trading off latency, cost, or auditability. Redwood gives you a predictable inference tier — fast, instrumented, and auditable — so you can ship features without building expensive infra."
- Positioning pillars: 1) Predictable TCO via batching/quantization playbooks + reserved capacity; 2) Compliance story: private deployment, KMS/HSM, audit logs; 3) Deterministic fallbacks and observability (tracing/token-level cost).
- Top competitor threats: single-vendor cloud AI (fast to onboard but opaque costs), boutique fraud-LM startups (vertical expertise), in-house infra (control).
- Differentiated plays: Sell reserved-capacity + compliance bundle; provide pre-built KYC/fraud prompt templates and eval suites; benchmarking kit vs cloud endpoints (latency/cost per 1M requests).
- Launch experiments (8 weeks): 1) Run a latency/cost comparison lab with 3 fintech pilot customers (Jira: GTM-231); 2) Hosted webinar with payments infra leads + benchmark results; 3) One-pager for procurement highlighting SLA & KMS.
- Early success metrics: Pilot adoption (3 signed pilots), delta in per-token cost vs cloud (-20%+ target), 99th percentile latency SLO demonstration.

2) Healthcare (clinical documentation, triage, coding)
- Core JTBD: accelerate clinician workflows (notes, coding, summarization) while ensuring PHI safeguards and audit trails.
- Archetype: Head of Clinical Informatics, platform teams at EHR integrators, health-tech startups.
- 3-line narrative: "Ship LLM-powered clinician workflows that protect patient data and enable auditability. Redwood offers private deployments, audit logging, and deterministic routing so health teams can automate without regulatory surprise."
- Pillars: 1) Private deployment + data residency; 2) Auditability + fine-grained access controls; 3) Integration-ready connectors (FHIR, HL7) and clinical eval recipes.
- Competitor threats: EHR vendor partners (native integrations), specialized clinical NLP vendors, conservative IT/security orgs.
- Differentiated plays: Create a healthcare compliance play pack (SOC2 + HIPAA checklist + sample BAAs), FHIR connector examples, and an eval harness for clinical accuracy.
- Launch experiments: 1) Customer roundtable with 2 EHR partners to validate connectors; 2) Build BAA template and price pilot deals with private deployment add-on; 3) Host a security lab walkthrough for infosec buyers.
- Early metrics: Signed BAA pilots, time-to-integration (target: <6 weeks), false-positive rate on key clinical prompts.

3) Legal (contracts, discovery, regulatory research)
- Core JTBD: speed up contract review, extract obligations, and support legal ops with explainable outputs and audit trails.
- Archetype: Legal ops lead, GC at startups and mid-market, document review vendors.
- Narrative: "Cut review time without losing explainability — Redwood delivers inference with provenance, role-based access, and deterministic reruns for legal evidence."
- Pillars: 1) Explainability & provenance (token-level outputs, traceability); 2) Private deployment + data retention controls; 3) Accuracy guardrails and prompt/eval templates for contract language.
- Competitor threats: Legal-specific AI tools (fast vertical features), internal vendors used by law firms.
- Differentiated plays: Provide contract QA starter pack (prebuilt extraction prompts + eval corpus), feature highlighting output provenance and rerunability for audits.
- Launch experiments: 1) Pilot with 2 legal ops teams on NDA/contract extraction; 2) Generate a legal-ops ROI calculator showing review time reduction.
- Metrics: reduction in reviewer-hours, accuracy of extracted clauses, repeatable provenance checks.

4) Enterprise SaaS (embedded product features)
- Core JTBD: add LLM features into existing product interfaces while controlling unit economics and maintaining consistent UX performance.
- Archetype: Product manager / platform engineer at SaaS companies (CRM, analytics, HR tools).
- Narrative: "Add reliable, low-latency LLM features without ballooning cost or increasing incident surface. Redwood gives product teams deterministic inference and cost controls so they can ship ML features fast."
- Pillars: 1) Developer ergonomics & API parity across environments; 2) Cost controls (caching, batching, quantization recommendations); 3) Rollouts & fallbacks (canary/A-B, automatic fallback policies).
- Competitor threats: Low-friction public APIs (fastest to prototype), model marketplaces, and internal infra teams.
- Differentiated plays: SDKs and quickstarts for common product flows (search augmentation, helpdesk summaries), pre-configured rollout templates, and cost-savings calculators for PMs.
- Experiments: 1) Product toolkit: 3 SDK examples + starter prompts (support bot, summarizer, contextual search); 2) Run small customer workshops showing cost delta vs naive endpoint use.
- Metrics: number of PM-led pilots, percent reduction in per-feature token spend, dev time to integration.

5) Government & Defense (procurement, situational awareness)
- Core JTBD: provide robust, audited inference for sensitive workflows with strict compliance, offline/air-gapped deployments, and accredited security posture.
- Archetype: Gov procurement leads, defense integrators, platform security teams.
- Narrative: "Deliver inference with an operations model that meets procurement controls and classification requirements. Redwood supports private/on-prem deployments and an audit-first control plane so agencies can adopt LLMs safely."
- Pillars: 1) Accreditation-friendly deployments (air-gap, on-prem package); 2) Strong identity/KMS/HSM integrations and long audit-retention; 3) Procurement-friendly pricing (contracts, reserved capacity).
- Competitor threats: Defense contractors (custom integrations), cloud vendors with gov-only zones, specialized accredited vendors.
- Differentiated plays: Packaging for procurement: statements of work, compliance artifacts, and an on-prem quickstart. Pilot with a defense integrator partner.
- Experiments: 1) Create an on-prem quickstart + architecture whitepaper; 2) Run a procurement mock-eval with security team.
- Metrics: procurement checklist pass-rate, pilot contracting velocity, successful on-prem deploy.

Cross-vertical asks for product / security teams:
- Easier BAA/SLA templates and a checklist for SOC2 + HIPAA + FedRAMP talking points.
- A benchmarking kit (scripts + dashboards) for latency/cost vs major cloud endpoints and self-hosted infra.
- A set of vertical prompt/eval corpora (small seed datasets) to demonstrate accuracy and regressions.

Open questions & risks:
- How many vertical-specific templates can we reasonably maintain without fragmenting the product? (ops cost tradeoff).
- Procurement cycle for gov and healthcare is long; what is the acceptable pilot length before we move to PE/sales engagement?
- Regulatory prohibitions in some markets (e.g., EU data residency nuance) — clarify product-level guarantees.

Immediate next steps (owners & tickets):
- Build fintech benchmark kit (owner: Jared Lee, ticket: GTM-231).
- Draft healthcare BAA + security lab script (owner: Marta Alvarez, ticket: SEC-88).
- Legal pilot outreach list + contract extraction seed data (owner: Tom Chen, ticket: CS-147).
- Enterprise SaaS SDK examples + cost calculator (owner: Priya Khanna, ticket: DEVX-99).
- On-prem quickstart whitepaper (owner: Hannah O'Rourke, ticket: ENG-510).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive and prioritizes experiments that validate buyer economics and procurement blockers. Feedback: which vertical should get a headcount-backed pilot push next quarter?
- Please add any direct competitor wins/losses you have from customers and flag follow-up items into the linked Jira tickets.
